title: cf-stability: string stability of learned car-following models
description: Code, configurations, run manifests and results of the study "String Stability of Learned Car-Following Models: Audit, Differentiable Penalties, a Certified Hybrid and Corridor-Level Validation" (Mathematics 2026, 14(22), 4152, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14224152): an audit of the equilibrium (string) stability of learned car-following models, differentiable stability penalties, a residual hybrid with an a priori certificate, and the validation of the laws on SUMO corridors of NGSIM I-80 and US-101. The archive holds the code, the published tables, figures and report, and the run outputs they are computed from (training-run metrics and audits, per-event closed-loop metrics, corridor-run metrics and the compact speed fields of the figures, scenarios, law files, calibrations and fold definitions). The raw data, the extracted events and the simulated trajectories are not included; the README (section Reproduce) gives the three levels of reproduction and the data access steps.

notes: The code, the configurations and the documentation are under the MIT licence. The run outputs computed from third-party data are not: NOTICE.md reports the terms of each data provider, as read on 16 November 2026, and the files computed from each source, and it does not merge these terms into one licence. The corridor scenario files hold NGSIM data in adapted form and are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0. Every file with highD-derived events in its provenance (the checkpoints trained on them, the checkpoints fine-tuned from these on NGSIM, the corridor laws and results built from them, the metrics) is provided for non-commercial research and teaching only: the highD terms allow no commercial use of a derivative work. The IDM parameters fitted on the Waymo car-following pairs and the metrics computed on them are released under the Waymo Dataset License Agreement for Non-Commercial Use (https://waymo.com/open/terms/; copy in WAYMO_OPEN_DATASET_LICENSE.txt). The files computed from OpenACC follow CC BY 4.0. No data of highD or of the Waymo Open Dataset is included. From version 2.2.4 the segment and vehicle labels of the Waymo car-following pairs are not distributed: the fold definitions of the pairs are not in the archive, and the per-event tables of the pairs name events and followers by ordinal numbers (README, section Data access).
